findings.claim: AvgJoesCrypto (AJC): long-running crypto educator/analyst (Substack 'The Average Joe's Crypto' since ~2022 on Arbitrum, Curve wars, ve(3,3); FrenTechDAO), described in results as Blockworks-affiliated; asked publicly how to bridge to Robinhood Chain in July 2026. #6 on fomo 7d/30d/all ($3.1M/$3.76M/$3.97M; 91.5K fomo followers; 810 trades, $1.82M volume, 43 holdings). No evidence of token launches, clans, or dump accusations found.
findings.evidence: Substack posts; X post 'How do I bridge to Robinhood chain?'; local leaderboard JSON.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: DeFi-native analyst who moved into Robinhood Chain memes early (July) and sized well; relatively low trade count for high PnL implies a few good early entries. Candidate for 'early-mover on new chain' cohort; check whether entries cluster in the first days of RH Chain launches.

findings.claim: frogmanhaha (Frogman; X @frogmanhaha / @frogmanhaha_): #7 on fomo 30d/all ($3.68M; 45.3K fomo followers) with an EVM-only wallet, only 227 trades and $21.9K cumulative volume — PnL/volume ~168x, so nearly all PnL is unrealized on very early buys. X profile says portfolio 'will either go to $0 or $3M by end of year'; posts describe buying 0.5% of a coin's supply at ~$60K mcap, sitting on $700K+ unrealized, then buying back at $120M-$200M mcap; publicly shills $CASHCAT and $AI, and offered $500 to anyone who suggests his next 10x. Featured in fomo's 'Weekly Top Trades'. No evidence of launching tokens or running clans.
findings.evidence: X profile/search snippets for @frogmanhaha and @frogmanhaha_; local leaderboard JSON (wallets.solana = null, trades 227, volume $21.9K).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Textbook 'one early CASHCAT/AI bag' leaderboard entrant; explicitly gambling (0 or $3M). Not a copy target; his public calls to followers (with cash bounties for suggestions) make him a hype amplifier whose posts could be used as a contrarian/late-cycle indicator.

findings.claim: change (X @changefomo, 14.9K X followers; bio 'Qui totum vult totum perdit', link fomo.family/r/change): 337.5K fomo followers; #8 all-time ($3.40M) but #85 7d / #37 30d; the highest-churn profile in the set after frankdegods (2,712 trades, $27.4M volume, PnL/volume 0.12x, 26 holdings). Listed in the KuCoin top-10 fomo KOLs by 7D PnL. A Solana pump.fun token 'ChangeFomo' exists (likely fan/derivative). His X content is motivational ('grind during the quiescence... harvest during euphoria') rather than coin calls; he promotes a fomo referral link.
findings.evidence: X search result for @changefomo (bio, follower count, referral link); solanatracker 'ChangeFomo' token page; KuCoin KOL list; local leaderboard JSON.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Active, high-volume trader whose PnL is mostly realized and whose fomo audience (337K) dwarfs his X audience (15K) — i.e., a fomo-native KOL whose buys are visible to a large in-app crowd. Referral-fee income (25% of referees' fees) is a documented secondary revenue source for such accounts. Good candidate for measuring follower-flow price impact after his buys.

findings.claim: notanicecat69 (Wood): Solana memecoin trader profiled in a fomo AMA; rebuilt from ~$4K (1 ETH + 1 NFT) to seven figures via GoFX (20x) and WIF; sold enough by Feb 2025 to cover years of expenses and moved mostly to cash by March 2025. Stated rules: wait 48h+ after launch ('new pairs are a game rigged against you'), narrative/one-sentence-thesis selection, 2-3 tokens max, only 2.5% of net worth in the hot wallet, sell incrementally into strength, keep a moon bag, never re-enter an exited coin. findings.claim: CROSS-CUTTING: The Robinhood Chain memecoin cohort's biggest winners are all launch-window entries into a few tokens (CASHCAT via Noxa; PONS launchpad token; AI and BONER via LONG stock-pairs; MARSCOIN), and the documented mechanics favor insiders/early wallets: CASHCAT's five most profitable wallets took ~$3.7M against ~12,300 sell orders; its main Uniswap pool held only ~$6.6M liquidity at ~$150M cap; Noxa (75% of deployments) shut down 11 days after launch and redirected 100% of fees to creators (called a 'soft rug'); LONG pairs showed reflexive stock-token liquidity depletion (HIMS 2x premium). Copy-trade caveats from KuCoin/Odaily guides: signals arrive late (often +10-20%), clan/leaderboard PnL 'may be carried by one or two large positions', use fomo as an 'alpha radar' not 'copy homework'.
findings.evidence: crypto.news CASHCAT explainer; news.bitcoin.com CASHCAT liquidity figures; CoinGape/crypto.news Noxa collapse; CoinEx BONER analysis; KuCoin/Odaily practical guides; Datawallet and CoinCodex reviews (0.5% fee, min $0.95; sell-side failures reported).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: A retail-executable strategy cannot rely on being first into launches (insiders/snipers own that) or on mirroring KOLs (late, and KOLs sell into followers). The remaining testable edges are (a) post-launch survivor selection (Wood's 48h rule), (b) launchpad/venue-token and stock-paired-meta plays (PONS, LONG pairs) entered on fundamentals, and (c) short-horizon KOL-flow front-running, which must clear ~1%+0.5%x2 round-trip fees plus price impact.

findings.claim: fomo's follow/alert system is manual notification-based (no auto-copy). Six notification classes exist: Price alerts, Friends' activity (buys/sells of followed accounts, filterable by minimum trade size e.g. $1,000), Trending activity (fires when 'a certain coin is being bought by a lot of traders'), Top traders' activity ('large trades made by the top traders'), Announcements, New followers. Push-notification types visible via fomoapi include LARGE_BUY, LARGE_SELL, NEW_LISTING, PRICE_SINCE_LISTED, TRADE_COMMENT_ADDED, FOLLOWED.
findings.evidence: fomo's own blog 'Leveraging fomo's Social Features' enumerates the six notification categories and the trade-size filter; fomobyte guide describes 'Trade Alerts' feed and manual copy flow; Datawallet: 'Fomo should not be confused with automated copy trading... you still decide manually whether to act on it'; fomoapi.io docs list the /v2/notifications notificationType values and alert types buy/sell/thesis/whale/price/trade/follow with source=feed|push.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Defines exactly which events reach the crowd and when: a strategy can target the moment a 'Trending activity'/'multi-user trade' or 'Top trader large buy' push fires, and size trades above the followers' common $-filters to be visible (or below them to stay invisible).

findings.claim: The 'follower flow pushes price, caller sells into it' mechanism is widely asserted by credible observers and implicitly acknowledged by fomo itself, but no one has published a quantified event study (price impact in the minutes after a KOL buy on fomo).
findings.evidence: DWF Ventures study (reported 28 Aug 2026): 'If a prominent account buys a relatively illiquid token before its followers, subsequent purchases can push the price higher, giving the original trader a better entry price than the people trying to replicate the trade'; 'followers may effectively provide the liquidity needed for the exit'; 'the flywheel growth effect is a double-edged sword'; but 'the data does not establish that popular traders intentionally trade against followers.' fomoscan: 'By the time a trade is visible, posted and copied, the person you are copying may already be selling into the flow your copy created.' fomo's own help page lists as a red flag traders who 'promote tokens after buying and sell as followers buy in.' Bankless: traders can 'dump on followers', 'build a position before calling it' (bundling), buy through one wallet and sell through another. X post by Solo Top (24 Aug 2026, ~6.8k views): 'KOLs buy small market cap memes -> FOMO followers buy too -> price spikes immediately -> KOLs take profits -> FOMO followers buy at the peak.'
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Core thesis of the 'social signal' edge is consistent with what practitioners and DWF describe, but the magnitude/duration of the follower-driven spike is unmeasured; must be estimated from our own on-chain data (KOL buy timestamp vs subsequent fomo-relayed buys and pool price).

findings.claim: Base rates for fomo copy-followers are dismal: DWF Ventures found only 6.16% of ~292,000 fomo wallets had positive realized PnL over 90 days; only 25 wallets netted >$10k realized. DWF attributes this to execution asymmetry ('followers receive signals seconds or minutes after original traders') and the exit-liquidity structure, not chance.
findings.evidence: Yellow.com (author Murtuza Merchant, 28 Aug 2026) and AlexaBlockchain summaries of DWF Ventures research; an X post surfaced in search cites the same 292,531-wallet figure with an estimated $1.26B buyer loss (that number was only seen in a search snippet, not verified).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Confirms that naively 'buying what X buys' after the app alert is negative-EV at scale; any edge must come from being earlier than the alert (on-chain detection) or from exiting into the follower wave rather than joining it.

findings.claim: fomoapi.io sells two WebSocket feeds: /ws/alerts (app feed, 'the same moment the app shows it'; free tier 15s delayed, keyless 60s delayed) and /ws/trades (Growth $499/mo+), an on-chain stream it advertises as 'about 15 seconds before the app shows it — the window to act before the crowd sees the alert'. Messages carry txHash, block, blockTs, seenAt, latencyMs (example 1100 ms after block timestamp), trader wallet+handle, token mcap, side, usdValue, and a 'verified' field (db=resolved fomo trader, relay=routing layer, code=pending) with possible retractions. Only Robinhood Chain and Solana are covered by /ws/trades.
findings.evidence: fomoapi.io/docs schema and plan table (Free 10k req/mo; Starter $49; Growth $499 with /ws/trades; Scale custom). The ~15 s lead is a vendor claim; no independent measurement of the fomo app's indexer lag was found. Related: fomoscope.xyz advertises '15 sec refresh' of fomo data ($20-35/mo).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: If the ~15 s app lag is real, an on-chain watcher (own node/sequencer feed or fomoapi Growth) can enter after a KOL's block and before the crowd's push notification; the 'verified' field and retractions imply wallet-to-handle resolution is probabilistic, so false positives must be handled.

findings.claim: On Robinhood Chain (chain id 4663) trades are relayed: users do not submit their own transactions. Five relayer addresses submit 70.2% of all trades; the largest (0xcaf681a6…5cb2) submitted 18.4M trades on behalf of 469,815 distinct traders and one address alone submits 25% of trades. Bitquery found genuine sandwich/arb extraction is negligible (~$599k over 13 days, ~1 dollar per 20,000 traded); apparent front-running patterns were router order-splitting artifacts. Memecoins are 93.5% of chain volume with a 51.1% round-trip win rate.
findings.evidence: Bitquery investigation 'What 63 million trades reveal about Robinhood Chain'. Combined with fomo's disclosure that 'one in every two active wallets' on Robinhood Chain comes from fomo (ChainCatcher) and fomo's ~64k daily active addresses / ~$101M daily volume (36% of terminal volume), the dominant relayer is plausibly fomo's, but that attribution is not stated by Bitquery (speculation, low confidence).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Filtering on the fomo relayer's from-address (or the relay contract) gives a chain-speed, app-independent view of ALL fomo user flow into a Pons pool—i.e., a direct measure of the follower wave in real time, and a cheap way to detect KOL entries before the app alert. Sandwich risk to our own entries is low.

findings.claim: On Solana every fomo trade is co-signed by a single infrastructure wallet tagged 'Fomo Co-signer' on Solscan (AgmLJBMDCqWynYnQiPCuj9ewsNNsBJXyzoUhD9LJzN51), which 'shows up on almost every token'; routing goes through DFlow. fomo charges a $0.95 minimum per transaction on top of 0.5%, so a $20 copy trade pays ~4.75% one way (~9.5% round trip).
findings.evidence: X thread by Geta-bōshi (16 Jun 2026) on the co-signer; MASTR post (9 Aug 2026) documenting co-signer + fee vault with visible $0.95 transfers and DFlow /order and /intent routing; insights4vc confirms '$0.95 minimum per transaction'.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Solana analogue of the relayer signal: subscribe to the co-signer's transactions to see fomo flow at chain speed. The $0.95 minimum means small followers are heavily fee-taxed and their 'trending' waves are fee-inefficient; it also caps how small a fomo-executed scalp can be.

findings.claim: Robinhood Chain infrastructure timing: ~100 ms (sub-second, irregular) blocks; first-come-first-served sequencer with no public mempool; a public sequencer feed (wss://feed.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com) broadcasts ordered transactions before RPC nodes re-execute blocks, and Chainstack explicitly lists 'copy-trading signal detection' as a use case while noting 'there is nothing to front-run… the feed reports what the sequencer has already decided.' Glassnode measured submission latency of 3 ms from AWS Ohio vs 200 ms from Sydney (~2 blocks).
findings.evidence: chainstacklabs/robinhood-chain-sequencer-feed README; QuickNode Robinhood Chain guide (feed URLs, FCFS, sub-second irregular blocks); Kucoin flash on 100 ms blocks; CryptoTimes summary of Glassnode latency probes (13 Jul 2026); Robinhood docs on FCFS ordering.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: A retail-executable bot can read the free sequencer feed from a US-East box and react to a KOL's fomo buy within ~1 block, well ahead of a ~15 s app alert; running from Ohio/Virginia matters. Pons' 2-block launch protection is irrelevant here since the signal is post-launch.

findings.claim: Practitioner playbooks emphasize the delay and 'buy flat, not vertical': an Odaily guide advises filtering alerts to 'Trades, Theses, Multi-user trades, New traders', checking a trader's last 20 trades, and 'FOMO's signals reach you with a delay. First compare their entry price with the current price; if it's already pumped 10%-20%, this is essentially not the same trade anymore.' Bankless describes following friends to 'tail or counter-trade'. App Store reviewers report 3-5 s execution delays that worsen average entry.
findings.evidence: Odaily 'FOMO Practical Guide: From Finding People to Finding Coins'; Bankless 'Trading in Public with FOMO'; Apple App Store review 'Delays' (3-5 second buy/sell delay). No X thread by a fomo KOL explicitly describing 'sell into the followers' as their own playbook was found; the closest are third-party warnings (Solo Top, fomoscan, Moby: traders may 'front-run their own followers').
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Suggests the crowd's own heuristic (skip if +10-20% already) which bounds the follower wave: followers chase only the first ~10-20% move, so a fade/exit should target that band; the 3-5 s in-app execution lag is an additional handicap for app-executed copying versus direct on-chain execution.

findings.claim: Copy signals can be spoofed: 'copy trading Fomo + Pumpfun app traders can get spoofed: fake tx on top, wrong buy, you follow bait, rekt'; Bloom Trading built detection of the real trader address behind fomo/pump app accounts. Independent wallet-resolution tools (fomoscan: >1M handle-to-wallet links plus follower graph; fomowalletfinder; fomotags; open-source YvesxDev/fomo-wallet-resolver which uses fomo's internal profile API + an unsigned USDC transfer to reveal the Solana wallet, and Relay bridge history to match EVM wallets) exist because fomo hides wallet addresses.
findings.evidence: Potion X post (26 Aug 2026, 15.9k views); fomoscan.sh and its copy-trading page (survivor bias, hidden wallets, 'concentrated, sudden follower growth' as a red flag); GitHub README of fomo-wallet-resolver.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Any KOL-following signal must be built on resolved wallets (not app handles) and should discount traders with sudden follower spikes or multi-wallet behavior; the same resolver approach can be used to map the leaderboard to on-chain addresses for the backtest.

findings.claim: Robinhood Chain (chain id 4663) is an Arbitrum Nitro/Orbit L2 with ETH gas, ~100 ms blocks (measured 104.3 ms average since Jul 1), a single first-come-first-served sequencer in AWS us-east-2 (Ohio), and NO priority-fee ordering: paying more gas cannot move you ahead in the queue.
findings.evidence: Official docs: 'first-come, first-served sequencing model, where the order is determined strictly by the arrival time at the sequencer... no transaction can bypass others by paying higher fees.' Robinhood spec cites 100 ms blocks; Arbitrum Foundation blog says ~250 ms; my own RPC read (block 53,886,180 at ts 1788486553, chain launched Jul 1 00:00 UTC) gives 104.3 ms/block. Glassnode probes: sequencer at sequencer.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com in AWS Ohio.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Execution edge on Robinhood Chain is purely network latency to Ohio, not fee bidding. A retail bot on a us-east-2 VPS is structurally faster than any Telegram bot or app user elsewhere; fee-based sniping (Solana Jito tips) has no analogue here.

findings.claim: Geographic latency to the sequencer ranges from 3 ms (Ohio) to 200 ms (Sydney), i.e. ~2 blocks of ordering edge for a colocated bot; the app-level fomo feed is reported to lag chain by ~15 s.
findings.evidence: Glassnode measurements reported Jul 13 2026: Ohio 3 ms, Virginia 18 ms, Chicago 27 ms, London 91 ms, Tokyo 140 ms, Sydney 200 ms; '197 ms difference... almost two blocks worth of edge'. fomoapi.io sells an on-chain WSS stream described as '~15s ahead of the app' (Growth tier $499+/mo).
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Copy-trading fomo leaderboard wallets via the app feed means entering ~15 s (≈150 blocks) after the leader; on a 1%-fee, thin-liquidity Pons pool that lag is usually fatal for scalps. Any copy strategy must source signals on-chain (sequencer feed or WSS logs), not from the app feed.

findings.claim: Robinhood publishes a PUBLIC sequencer feed (wss://feed.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com) that broadcasts ordered transactions with calldata before RPC nodes finish executing them, giving ~50-130 ms of lead over standard RPC/WSS log subscriptions. Because ordering is already fixed when you see a tx, you can back-run/copy it but cannot sandwich or front-run it.
findings.evidence: Chainstack's open-source decoder README: 'the sequencer announces that decision on one WebSocket, carrying the ordering and the calldata but no result'; lead over nodes is 'their re-execution time—typically 50-130 milliseconds'; decode cost ~4 µs basic / ~70 µs with sender recovery; examples include copy-trading signals. Docs confirm no public mempool and FCFS ordering.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: This is the fastest legal retail signal source for copying a specific wallet on Robinhood Chain: decode the leader's buy from the feed, submit your own within one or two blocks. It also means sandwich MEV against your own trades is structurally impossible on this chain (unlike Solana/ETH), so 'anti-MEV' features of bots are marketing here.

findings.claim: Gas on Robinhood Chain is negligible: live baseFee 0.33 gwei (read Sep 4 2026); a swap of 135k-250k gas costs ~0.00004-0.00008 ETH ≈ $0.11-$0.21 at $2,500 ETH. A July 15 measured single-leg swap used 135,568 gas at 0.068 gwei ≈ $0.02.
findings.evidence: eth_gasPrice = 0x136a7d50 (325,483,856 wei) and latest block baseFeePerGas = 329,960,000 wei from rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com; Splitshot blog measured 135,568 gas @ ~0.068 gwei = ~0.0000092 ETH on Jul 15; Arbitrum Foundation cites median fee ~$0.00127/tx.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Gas is a rounding error (<0.1% of a $500 trade). Round-trip cost is dominated by the 1% Pons hook/pool fee per leg plus venue fee plus your own price impact; there is no economic reason to batch or hesitate on gas.

findings.relevance_to_strategy: A retail user can run a full bot with viem/ethers + one $49/mo RPC plan: subscribe to logs or the sequencer feed, quote via QuoterV2 (V1 tokens) or the V4 Quoter (graduated V2 tokens), and swap via SwapRouter02 / UniversalRouter. No permissioned relay is required.

findings.claim: CORRECTION TO PREMISE: Pons V1 (fixed-supply straight-to-Uniswap-V3, 1% pool fee, 2-block protection) is DISABLED for new launches; all new Pons launches since ~Aug 3 use V2: a constant-product bonding curve (phantom quote 1.68 ETH, graduation at 4.2 ETH, 1B supply, 1% curve fee) that graduates into a Uniswap V4 full-range pool with 0 LP fee and a 1% hook fee. V1 tokens already launched still trade on their V3 1% pools.
findings.evidence: On-chain reads Sep 4 2026: V1 factory 0xA5aAb3F0…351feB launchEnabled()=false (launchConfig: graduationThreshold 4.2 ETH, maxWalletBps 500, maxTxBps 550, restrictionBlocks 2; dex poolFee 10000=1%, tickSpacing 200). V2 factory 0x7eD598Bc…1EC7e launchEnabled()=true, launchFee 0.0005 ETH, launchConfig 0: supply 1e9, curveFeeBps 100, phantomQuote 1.68e18, graduationThreshold 4.2e18, poolFee 0, tickSpacing 200. Hook 0xE5e70264…e044: hookFeeBps 100, protocolFeeShareBps 3000, buybackBurnBps 5000, maxInternalPriceImpactBps 300. Defiant: V2 contracts shipped Aug 3; V1 still collected $508k of Pons' $4.89M fees on Aug 31.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Any backtest built on 'V3 pool from block 1, 2-block protection' only describes July-early-August tokens. Current flow is pump.fun-like: 99% of tokens die on the curve, and post-graduation liquidity is a hook-gated V4 pool that some external bots cannot trade until graduation. Strategy must be split into curve-phase and pool-phase regimes.

findings.claim: Pons V2 launch protection is a time-based snipe tax, not a block window: buys in the first 3 seconds (on-chain snipeTaxSeconds=3; docs say 5 s) pay a 99% tax decaying exponentially to 0 (docs: ~25% at 1 s, ~3% at 2 s). Launcher/creator plus up to 32 named wallets are exempt, so dev bundles get the opening price while outsiders cannot.
findings.evidence: V2 factory snipeTaxStartBps()=9900, snipeTaxSeconds()=3 and identical values on 11 freshly deployed curve contracts (read Sep 4 2026). Docs: 'starts at 99% of a buy and decays exponentially to zero across the first 5 seconds... near 25% one second in and around 3% at two seconds'; exemptions immutable at creation. Bundler tools (Pons Bundler Bot) let launchers buy in the launch block across many wallets.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Block-0 sniping by outsiders is economically dead on Pons V2; the first seconds belong to the launcher's exempt wallets. A retail sniper's earliest sane entry is ~2-3 s post-launch, by which time bundled insiders hold the cheapest supply — a classic exit-liquidity setup that must be filtered on.

findings.claim: Pons V2 launch economics (computed from on-chain params at $2,500 ETH): opening market cap 1.68 ETH (~$4.2k); graduation at 12.25x the opening price with market cap ~20.6 ETH (~$51k); the graduated V4 pool is seeded with 4.2 ETH (~$10.5k) plus ~204M tokens, i.e. ~$21k displayed liquidity at graduation. 71.4% of supply is sold on the curve. Curves also launch against a USD stable (phantom $3,236 / threshold $8,090) and other pair tokens.
findings.evidence: phantomQuote 1.68e18, graduationThreshold 4.2e18, supply 1e9, reserved = supply*phantom/(phantom+threshold) = 28.6%; sampled curves show pairToken variants with 6-decimal reserves 3,236,000,000/8,090,000,000 and other token thresholds (24.94, 42.35, 119.9, 369 units). Docs: 'Every launch on the same settings graduates into a pool of the same size, at the same price'; graduation liquidity permanently locked.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: A '$50k-$500k liquidity' Pons token is a post-graduation pool that has already re-rated 2.4x-24x above graduation (full-range CP: quote side = displayed liq/2). Position sizing must be keyed to quote-side reserve: $5k into a $50k pool is a 20% average-slippage entry.

findings.claim: Realistic round-trip cost on a Pons token (constant-product full-range V4 pool; V1 V3 pools behave similarly): fee-only round trip is 1.99% via direct RPC (1% Pons per leg), 2.98% via fomo (0.5% app + 1% Pons per leg), 3.96% via GMGN/Maestro/NockBot (1% bot), 4.94% via a 1.5% snipe fee; gas adds ~$0.2-0.4. Adding your own price impact (entry slippage T/Q plus an equal exit impact): $500 in $50k liq ≈ 7.0% (fomo) / 8.0% (1% bot); $500 in $500k ≈ 3.4% / 4.4%; $2,000 in $100k ≈ 11.0% / 12.0%; $5,000 in $500k ≈ 7.0% / 8.0%; $5,000 in $50k ≈ 43% (uninvestable). Optional creator tax (up to 10%/leg) can add up to ~19% more; sampled launches mostly have 0%.
findings.evidence: Computed from on-chain hookFeeBps=100/curveFeeBps=100, sampled creatorTaxBps (10 of 11 recent curves = 0, one = 200 bps), maxCreatorTaxBps=1000, live gas 0.33 gwei, fomo fee ~0.5% (Datawallet), GMGN 1% on EVM (CoinCodeCap), Maestro 1% (CoinSpot/TelegramTrading), Banana Gun 0.5% manual / 1% snipe, NockBot 1%/1.5% (TradersDNA). CP math: avg execution price = spot*(1+T/Q); post-trade spot = spot*(1+T/Q)^2. Note fomo's mark-to-market PnL will show the (1+T/Q)^2 jump as unrealized gain immediately after a large buy.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: A strategy needs >3% (fomo) to >4% (Telegram bot) gross edge per round trip just to break even on fees, before impact; on sub-$100k pools, $2k+ clips cost 10%+. This also explains how leaderboard 'PnL' inflates: a single $5k buy into a $50k pool marks the whole bag up 44%.

findings.claim: Solana venue costs for comparison: pump.fun bonding curve 1.25%/leg (0.95% protocol + 0.30% creator), PumpSwap 0.25-0.30%/leg; bot/terminal fees 0.5% (Axiom, Photon, BullX, GMGN-on-Solana, Padre, MevX, Telemetry) or 1% (Trojan, BonkBot, Maestro, Banana Gun snipe); Jito tips/priority 0.005-0.01 SOL normal (~$0.5-1 at $103 SOL), 0.05-0.1 SOL for contested launches. Fee-only round trips: pump.fun curve + 0.5% bot ≈ 3.5%, PumpSwap + 0.5% bot ≈ 1.6%, +1% bot ≈ 2.6%.
findings.evidence: Pump.fun fee explainer (1.25% curve), PumpSwap 0.25% + 0.05% creator, solanatools fee table, Trojan/coinspot reviews on Jito tip ranges.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Post-graduation Solana (PumpSwap 0.25%) is roughly 2x cheaper per round trip than post-graduation Robinhood (Pons 1% hook), while Robinhood gas/tips are ~10x cheaper. Fee sensitivity favours high-turnover strategies on Solana and lower-turnover, larger-move strategies on Robinhood.

findings.claim: Retail terminals/bots that explicitly support Robinhood Chain as of Sep 2026: Axiom (added Jul 11; MEV-protection toggle, wallet tracker, limit orders, perps; ~0.75-1% with referral discounts), GMGN (web+app+TG; 1% fee on EVM chains; copy trade, launchpad sniper, auto TP/SL, wallet P&L), Maestro (TG; 1% with up to 30% volume cashback; copy trade 3 wallets free / 10 wallets on ~$200/mo Premium; trades Uniswap v2/v3/v4 and lists Pons among launchpad integrations), Banana Gun (TG bot only, not Banana Pro; day-1 Jul 10; 0.5% manual / 1% snipe; market, limit, copy), MevX (Robinhood among 6 chains), NockBot/NockTerminal (chain-native; 1% swap / 1.5% snipe; free screener with hook-gated-pool flags), fomo app (0.5%), Robinhood Wallet, Uniswap app. Photon is Solana-only; BullX/Trojan/BonkBot/Bloom/Sigma have no confirmed Robinhood support.
findings.evidence: Axiom integration articles; GMGN blog 'Robinhood Chain is live on GMGN'; CryptoPotato Maestro article; Banana Gun blog (Jul 10) and TechBullion (Jul 27); TelegramTrading MevX list; TradersDNA Nock write-up; telegramtrading GMGN vs Photon vs Axiom notes Photon Solana-only.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Off-the-shelf copy-trade automation on Robinhood Chain exists (GMGN, Maestro, Banana Gun, Axiom) at 1%/leg, i.e. ~4% round trip with Pons fees. None publishes latency; all are slower than a self-hosted us-east-2 bot on a FCFS chain.

findings.claim: No Robinhood-Chain trading bot publishes measured execution latency or an audited P&L track record. Banana Gun explicitly disclaims having a millisecond figure; Maestro/GMGN/Axiom make only qualitative 'fast' claims. Solana bots publish some numbers (Trojan 'sub-2-second' execution, 0.04 s price refresh; Photon ranked fastest in reviews) but likewise no audited returns.
findings.evidence: TechBullion on Banana Gun: 'It does not mean Banana Gun has published a matching millisecond figure of its own'; CryptoPotato Maestro piece: 'specific latency metrics aren't provided'; CoinCodeCap GMGN: 'no specific millisecond or latency guarantees'; parasol/rpcfast comparisons use star ratings only; Trojan reviews cite BOLT sub-2 s.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Vendor 'performance' cannot be used as an input; latency must be measured ourselves (sequencer-feed timestamp vs our tx inclusion block) and any copy-trade P&L must be simulated with explicit lag assumptions.

findings.claim: The only peer-reviewed-style evidence on memecoin copy-trading profitability finds thin margins: an LLM multi-agent KOL-selection framework evaluated on 6,000+ meme coins reports ~14% average return on identified smart-money trades but only ~3% per trade for the copier 'under realistic market frictions', with adversarial bots that front-run copiers, hide positions and fabricate sentiment.
findings.evidence: arXiv 2601.08641 (v3 Feb 2026): 'an average copier return of 3% per meme coin investment under realistic market frictions'; adversaries 'front-run trades, conceal positions, and fabricate sentiment, systematically extracting value from naïve copiers at scale'; EmergentMind summary cites 14% leader vs 3% copier.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: A 3%-per-trade copier edge is roughly equal to the fomo+Pons round-trip fee on Robinhood, so naive leaderboard copying is expected to net ~0 after costs; edge must come from lag reduction (sequencer feed) and leader/token filtering, not from copying per se.

findings.claim: Base rates: on Pons V2 I measured 636 launches vs 11 graduations in a 20,000-block (~35 min) window on Sep 4 2026 (≈18 launches/min, ~1.7% graduation ratio); third-party figures cite 1.10% lifetime and 1.27% for Aug 25-31 (83,962 launches / 1,064 graduations). On Solana, CoinGecko finds 68.7% of 18.7M pump.fun tokens have their last trade on launch day and ~1% graduate; a survival study of 832,941 launches (May-Jun 2026) finds 0.2% fast-regime graduation, 8.9x higher with a Telegram link.
findings.evidence: Own eth_getLogs counts of TokenLaunched (factory) and PoolGraduated (hook) topics; CoinGecko research; arXiv 2607.02823. The 1.10%/1.27% Pons figures appeared in search-engine summaries but I could not pin the hosting article (not in the MEXC or Bitget pieces I checked), so treat them as unattributed.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Any curve-phase strategy faces a ~98-99% dud rate; expected value must be carried by the ~1-2% that graduate, which argues for post-graduation entries (verified locked V4 liquidity) or extremely strict launcher/social filters.

findings.claim: Open-source retail tooling for Robinhood/Pons exists and is non-trivial: 'pons-sniper' (MIT, TypeScript; listens to V1+V2 factory events over WSS, V1 entries via exact-output V3 swaps in blocks N+1/N+2 within the 5%/5.5% caps, V2 entries on the curve with automatic snipe-tax verification, batch submission across many wallets, fixed or auto slippage 1-25%, TP/SL), 'pons-launch-engine' (launch+snipe your own token), 'robinhood-sniper-bot', 'robinhood-cli' (129 stars), 'robinhood-lp-bot', and Chainstack's sequencer-feed decoder.
findings.evidence: GitHub topic page lists repos and stars; pons-sniper README details detection/buy path/config; README warns 'Quotes and simulations reduce risk but cannot eliminate price movement, RPC failures, sequencer ordering, or contract risk.'
findings.relevance_to_strategy: A retail user does not need to write a sniper from scratch; the bigger implication is that these tools (plus bundlers) are already in the hands of launchers, so the earliest curve blocks are populated by multi-wallet insiders — a signal to detect (many exempt wallets, same-second buys) and avoid.

findings.claim: How to buy programmatically on Pons V2: pre-graduation call curve.buy(uint256 quoteIn, uint256 minTokensOut, address recipient) payable (send value = quoteIn for ETH pairs; approve the curve for ERC-20 pairs); quote off-chain from getReserves() (includes phantom quote) with fees applied on input for buys and on output for sells; call currentSnipeTaxBps(recipient) if within the first seconds; the final buy may be clamped to the reserved allocation so size minTokensOut from the rate. Post-graduation route through the Uniswap V4 PoolManager/UniversalRouter with the Pons hook (hook takes protocol fee + creator tax on the 'unspecified currency'). Index TokenLaunched (factory, indexed token/curve/deployer), CurveBuy/CurveSell (curve), PoolGraduated/PoolFeesSwept (hook). Public launching is currently whitelist-gated pending audits (three concurrent, none closed).
findings.evidence: Pons v2 docs integration sections; verified ABIs on Sourcify (factory: launchFee, pairTokenEconomics, canLaunch, snipeTax*; hook: hookFeeBps, protocolFeeShareBps, launches(bytes32)); curve selectors found in bytecode: buy(uint256,uint256,address), sell(uint256,uint256,address), getReserves(), realQuoteReserve(), currentSnipeTaxBps(address), creatorTaxBps(), feeBps(), graduated(), launchedAt(). Router 0xe33E9E479dF8802cb0866d5d05258bEc4cF62948 is a launch-and-buy router.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Everything needed for a self-hosted executor is public and verified; the curve is deterministic so quotes can be computed locally in microseconds, which matters on a FCFS chain where round-trips to a quoter cost blocks.

findings.claim: fomo.family execution and fees: ~0.5% per spot trade (0.45% base cited by one review; 10% referral discount; minimums on small sizes), gas sponsored via ERC-4337 account abstraction, self-custodial Privy embedded wallets with exportable keys, order handling via DFlow and cross-chain funding via Relay Protocol. Robinhood Chain support was announced ~Jul 10 2026. fomo's 'copy trading' is notification-based (you get an alert and choose to trade), not automatic mirroring.
findings.evidence: Datawallet: '~0.5% per trade... Network gas is sponsored by Fomo... DFlow for order handling... Relay's bridging infrastructure... keys can be exported'; coinspot/crowinvesting cite 0.45%-0.5%; fomo.family/answers: 'Copy trading gives you control—you decide whether to execute each trade'; Bitget news Jul 10 on Robinhood Chain support. Note: docs.onfomo.com (automatic copy trading with slots/leverage) is a DIFFERENT product (a Hyperliquid perp app), not fomo.family.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: Executing through fomo itself is the cheapest venue fee (0.5%) but is manual and app-lagged; a systematic strategy will run off-app with exported keys or a separate hot wallet, giving up the fee discount for latency and automation.

findings.claim: Third-party fomo data feeds: fomoapi.io (unofficial) offers REST + WSS: /ws/alerts (app feed: buys, sells, theses) and /ws/trades (on-chain stream). Free tier: 10k calls/mo, app feed realtime for 7 days then 15 s delayed, no on-chain stream; paid from $49/mo (24/7 realtime app feed); on-chain stream '~15s ahead of the app' only on Growth ($499+/mo). It lists Solana/ETH/Base/BSC/'Ronin (RH)'/Monad. fomoscope.xyz: REST only, 15 s refresh, $0 / $20 / $35 per 30 days at 30/60/100 req/min.
findings.evidence: fomoapi.io landing page endpoint and pricing tables; fomoscope.xyz pricing and FAQ.
findings.relevance_to_strategy: For Robinhood Chain the $499 on-chain stream is redundant: the same 'ahead of app' data is free from the public sequencer feed or a $49 WSS RPC, once leader wallets are resolved via the free tier's /v2/users/{handle}. Pay only for wallet resolution, not for the stream.

findings.claim: Wallet-tracking on Robinhood Chain: Arkham has an official partnership (labels, trader profiling, real-time alerts); Cielo (30+ chains), Nansen, GMGN and Axiom wallet trackers cover the chain; Nock Scout ranks wallets by realized profit with free chain-wide history; StalkChain publishes how-to guides. ## 2. Ranked strategy hypotheses

Target the crowd's own heuristic band (Odaily: skip if already +10-20%), i.e. exit at +8-15% or on time-stop.
- **Why it persists.** Structural: FCFS ordering + fomo's server-side feed lag + manual human copying. The lag cannot be arbitraged away by app users; fomo has no incentive to make the feed faster than its own indexer. Referral/Trader Rewards programs pay KOLs to broadcast, sustaining the wave.

Solana analogue via Helius on the "Fomo Co-signer" `AgmLJBM…zN51`.

## 3. Traps and pitfalls to audit

1. **Look-ahead via PnL fields.** fomoapi passes fomo's mark-to-market PnL; `unrealizedPnlUsd` at snapshot time embeds future prices. Recompute from trade prints and pool state at the time of each decision.
2. **Wallet-resolution look-ahead.** fomoapi `verified: db|relay|code` with retractions means handle→wallet mapping is probabilistic and may only be known after the fact. Backtest with the resolution state available at that timestamp.
3. **Survivorship in the leaderboard.** Top-100 is conditioned on winning; traders like Aurelius0121 fell out of 7d/30d. Use the full historical roster (peer.family polls every 5 min; our snapshots) not the current one.
4. **Regime in-sample.** Jul 1-Sep 3 is a launch + blow-off regime (volume 3x in the last week of August). Require the edge to survive July-only and August-only splits, and stress with 3-5x lower activity.
5. **Fee model.** Per-token `creatorTaxBps()`/`feeBps()` reads; V1 (1% V3 pool) vs V2 curve (1% on input) vs V2 v4 pool (1% hook on "unspecified currency" — verify whether exact-input buys pay in tokens); fomo $0.95 min on Solana; gas spikes to $60+/tx under congestion (Sep 1-2) and FCFS congestion shows up as failed/delayed inclusion, not a fee.
6. **Impact model.** Size to quote-side reserve, not market cap (liquidity/mcap of 2-5% is typical). Use constant-product for V2 v4 pools (full range) and tick-range math for V1 V3 pools. Our own buy marks up the bag by (1+T/Q)^2 — do not count that as PnL.
7. **Bot-polluted activity.** Exclude the top-5 relayer/bot addresses; dedupe by funding source; use net inflow, not counts.
8. **Ticker spoofing.** 361 contracts claimed "GME"; key everything by contract address.
9. **Signal spoofing.** Fake "fomo trader" txs and bait buys exist (Potion, Bloom); require the resolved wallet AND a matching feed item before acting, or size down on `code`-verified events.
10. **Latency assumptions.** All "~15 s" and "3 ms" figures are vendor/third-party; measure our own feed-to-inclusion latency from us-east-2 before trusting any timing-dependent PnL.
11. **Data-vendor conflicts.** fomo volume share (15% Dune vs 36% Chaincatcher vs $27M DefiLlama); Pons graduation stats (1.10%/1.27%) unattributed; DWF sample definition (fomo vs all Solana wallets). Prefer our own on-chain counts.
